title: From Counterfactual Edits to Human Narratives: LLM-Driven Interpretations for Recommender System Explanations
abstract: arXiv:2611.13914v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user's interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns

translated_title: 从反事实编辑到人类叙事：基于大语言模型的推荐系统解释诠释
translated_abstract: 推荐系统日益影响着用户在网上发现和消费的内容，但其输出背后的决策逻辑往往仍不透明。反事实解释（CFX）方法提供了一种有效途径，可以展示用户交互历史中的哪些改变会改变推荐结果。然而，在推荐场景中，CFX 通常需要多次编辑，产生冗长的、低层次（细粒度）的编辑列表，用户难以理解。此外，大多数评估侧重于编辑数量，而在很大程度上忽略了生成的 CFX 对用户来说是否连贯且可操作。我们认为，生成有效的 CFX 与传达模型行为之间的这一差距，源于缺乏以用户为中心的抽象以及有限的定性评估。为弥合这一差距，我们研究将大语言模型作为中介，把原始的 CFX 交互编辑列表总结为描述更高层次偏好模式的简洁自然语言解释。
tldr: 该论文提出利用大语言模型作为中介，将推荐系统反事实解释中冗长且难以理解的用户交互历史编辑列表，总结为描述高层偏好模式的简洁自然语言解释，从而弥合生成有效反事实解释与向用户传达模型行为之间的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using large language models as mediators to transform long, low-level counterfactual edit lists in recommender system explanations into concise natural language narratives describing higher-level preference patterns, bridging the gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior to users.
